history.period: 1880 CE (per Assam government; travel sites variously say 1931)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Thengal Bhawan is a 19th-century heritage mansion, not a temple. Built in 1880 by Raibahadur Siva Prasad Barooah, a wealthy tea planter and philanthropist, it was the family residence of the Barooah family at Jalukonibari village near Jorhat. Its fame rests on journalism, not worship: Barooah published a weekly Assamese newspaper in 1929 and then established his printing press and office here to publish 'Dainik Batori', the first Assamese daily newspaper — and, per the Assam government, the first daily in any language published from a village in India. Siva Prasad Barooah was owner and Bagmibar Nilamani Phukan the editor. The estate includes the main house, a guesthouse, a naamghar (Vaishnavite prayer hall), a tea garden, and a small museum; it now functions as a heritage guest house/museum. Conflicts in secondary sources: construction dated 1880 (govt) vs 1931 (travelsetu); Dainik Batori dated 1929/1933/1935 across sources — government version preferred here.

name: Thengal Bhawan
town_description: Jalukonibari is a village in Jorhat district, about 15 km southwest of Jorhat town, set among tea gardens; Thengal Bhawan stands here. Jorhat itself is upper Assam's cultural and tea capital on the south bank of the Brahmaputra.
tradition: Heritage (secular) — Neo-Vaishnavite cultural context via the estate's naamghar; not a temple

travel.railway: Jorhat Town railway station, about 15 km away
travel.road: Approach via Titabor/Jorhat road; local transport from Jorhat town

visitor_information.opening_hours: Mon-Sat 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; closed Sundays and some public holidays; entry approx INR 20 adult / INR 10 child (verify, per travelsetu)
